text_summary.body: From the twentieth to the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes, twelve years, Nehemiah as governor did not eat the governor's food; earlier governors had burdened the people with forty shekels and food; he did not buy land, kept his servants at the work, and fed 150 Jews and officials plus visitors daily.

setting.body: Years 20 and 32 of Artaxerxes I on Parker and Dubberstein's table; Cowley takes the 32nd year (433) as a fixed point, since Bigvai was governor by 408.

constraints.textual_assertion: from the twentieth year even to the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes
assumptions: Dated by its start (year 20 = 445/444); the governorship lasted to year 32 (433/432; Neh 13:6).

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik presents Nehemiah's refusal of the governor's allowance as an example of leadership by not taking.

open_questions: Who were "the former governors" (5:15)? Not identified in the sources read.
